text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Independent privatisation commission declines approval of government plan to privatise Thomson through a sale to Lagardere in which consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia would be sold to Korea's Daewoo. Committee opposes technology transfers linked to sale to Daewoo and lack of visibility on Daewoo's commitments. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis considered depriving Credit Foncier of the right to issue loans, ahead of a December 15 partial business takeover decision by Credit Immobilier de France.
-- Matif futures market chairman Gerard Pfauwadel unveils euro strategy and prepares switch to euro-denominated products.
LA TRIBUNE
-- General practitioners' and specialists' unions to negotiate separately with social security funds on sanctions against doctors who would break spending limits.
-- Aerospatiale seeks legal action court against Lagardere and Matra on grounds Matra broke an agreement with Aerospatiale on co-operation for Apache missiles by allying to British Aerospace.
-- Up to 1.8 million children in France live in poverty, survey shows.
-- Perfume retailer La Parfumerie to buy Marionnaud and become France's second largest retailer.
L'AGEFI
-- Government to start again a privatisation process for Thomson, renew talks with potential bidders.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- A return to investment is expected to fuel growth in 1997, after lacking in 1996, study shows.
-- Saudi prince Al-Waleed buys Paris hotel George V for 920 million francs.
-- National Assembly to approve 1996 budget modification bill today.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French authorities fear new terror attacks may follow bomb blast in a Paris suburban train on Tuesday that killed two and wounded over 100.
-- Daewoo Electronics president says he is "outraged" by France's backing out of Thomson privatisation.
